From: R. Okafor, Claims Operations Manager
To: All Claims Adjusters, Claims Assistants
Subject: Updated Service Level Agreement Targets and Escalation Paths

Effective 2023-09-01, the following service level targets apply to all
claims handled by the Great Lakes Mutual claims department. These
targets replace the interim guidelines issued on 2023-06-15 and
supersede the older expectations in the 2022 Claims Manual.

1. Initial contact with policyholder: within 1 business day of claim
   assignment.
2. Acknowledgement letter or email: within 2 business days of claim
   filing.
3. Field inspection scheduling: within 3 business days of claim
   assignment, unless the policyholder requests otherwise.
4. First inspection report submitted to file: within 5 business days
   of the inspection date.
5. Coverage determination (coverage letter issued): within 10
   business days of claim assignment for standard homeowner claims.
6. Estimate of damages completed: within 15 business days of claim
   assignment for claims under $25,000 in estimated damages.
7. Claim decision (approval or denial): within 30 calendar days of
   claim assignment for all claims, unless state law or policy
   language requires a different timeline.

Escalation: If any of the above deadlines cannot be met, the assigned
adjuster must notify their supervisor before the deadline passes and
log a note in the claim file explaining the reason for the delay and
the expected completion date. Supervisors are responsible for
reviewing the weekly aging report and following up on any claim that
exceeds 20 business days without a coverage determination.

Questions regarding these targets should be directed to me or to
J. Alvarez in Claims Compliance.

RECORD 2.21 — INTERNAL MEMO — PHOTO DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------

Date: 2023-08-04
From: L. Tran, Field Operations Supervisor
To: All Field Adjusters
Subject: Reminder — Photo Standards for Inspection Reports

A reminder that all inspection reports submitted on or after
2023-08-15 must include digital photographs that meet the following
minimum standards. Reports missing any required photo will be
returned to the adjuster for correction before the report is
accepted into the claim file.

Required photos per inspection type:

- Exterior inspection (dwelling): minimum 12 photos, including one
  photo of each elevation (front, rear, left, right), roof (if
  accessible), and any visible damage.
- Interior inspection: minimum 8 photos per affected room,
  including wide-angle shots and close-ups of any damage.
- Detached structure (garage, shed, etc.): minimum 4 photos,
  including one of the structure from each corner.
- Contents inventory: photographs of each room where contents are
  located, plus close-ups of any high-value items.

Photo quality: Each photo must be in focus, properly lit, and
time-stamped by the camera. Photos must be named using the claim
number and a sequence number (e.g., CL-2023-04512_01.jpg). Do not
use a photo that does not clearly show the damage or condition being
documented.

When uploading photos to the claim file, please verify that they
have been attached to the correct claim and that the file names
match the claim number. Duplicate or misnamed photos slow down the
review process.

RECORD 2.20 — INTERNAL MEMO — CLAIMS PROCESSING SLAs

Date: 2023-08-04
From: R. Okafor, Claims Operations Manager
To: All Claims Adjusters, Claims Assistants
Subject: Updated Service Level Agreement Targets and Escalation Paths

Effective 2023-09-01, the following service level targets apply to all
claims handled by the Great Lakes Mutual claims department. These
targets replace the interim guidelines issued on 2023-06-15 and
supersede the older expectations in the 2022 Claims Manual.

1. Initial contact with policyholder: within 1 business day of claim
   assignment.
2. Acknowledgement letter or email: within 2 business days of claim
   filing.
3. Field inspection scheduling: within 3 business days of claim
   assignment, unless the policyholder requests otherwise.
4. First inspection report submitted to file: within 5 business days
   of the inspection date.
5. Coverage determination (coverage letter issued): within 10
   business days of claim assignment for standard homeowner claims.
6. Estimate of damages completed: within 15 business days of claim
   assignment for claims under $25,000 in estimated damages.
7. Claim decision (approval or denial): within 30 calendar days of
   claim assignment for all claims, unless state law or policy
   language requires a different timeline.

Escalation: If any of the above deadlines cannot be met, the assigned
adjuster must notify their supervisor before the deadline passes and
log a note in the claim file explaining the reason for the delay and
the expected completion date. Supervisors are responsible for
reviewing the weekly aging report and following up on any claim that
exceeds 20 business days without a coverage determination.

Questions regarding these targets should be directed to me or to
J. Alvarez in Claims Compliance.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
RECORD 2.21 — INTERNAL MEMO — PHOTO DOCUMENTATION REQUIREMENTS
--------------------------------------------------------------------

Date: 2023-08-04
From: L. Tran, Field Operations Supervisor
To: All Field Adjusters
Subject: Reminder — Photo Standards for Inspection Reports

A reminder that all inspection reports submitted on or after
2023-08-15 must include digital photographs that meet the following
minimum standards. Reports missing any required photo will be
returned to the adjuster for correction before the report is
accepted into the claim file.

Required photos per inspection type:

- Exterior inspection (dwelling): minimum 12 photos, including one
  photo of each elevation (front, rear, left, right), roof (if
  accessible), and any visible damage.
- Interior inspection: minimum 8 photos per affected room,
  including wide-angle shots and close-ups of any damage.
- Detached structure (garage, shed, etc.): minimum 4 photos,
  including one of the structure from each corner.
- Contents inventory: photographs of each room where contents are
  located, plus close-ups of any high-value items.

Photo quality: Each photo must be in focus, properly lit, and
time-stamped by the camera. Photos must be named using the claim
number and a sequence number (e.g., CL-2023-04512_01.jpg). Do not
use a photo that does not clearly show the damage or condition being
documented.

When uploading photos to the claim file, please verify that they
have been attached to the correct claim and that the file names
match the claim number. Duplicate or misnamed photos slow down the
review process.
